lines.text: Every flying machine comes with a manual.
This one is for a rocket that hasn't flown.
Project 33 lives on a workbench, and this manual authorizes no ignition, no propulsion, and no flight.
lines.say: Project thirty-three lives on a workbench. And this manual authorizes no ignition, no propulsion, and no flight.

lines.text: Flight characteristics: not measured.
Performance data: not measured.
Here, that isn't a gap. It's the status.
Project 33 has four subsystems: the airframe, the rocket's flight computer, the launcher, and a laptop dashboard.
lines.say: Project thirty-three has four subsystems: the airframe, the rocket's flight computer, the launcher, and a laptop dashboard.

lines.text: The dashboard talks to the launcher over Wi-Fi.
lines.say: The dashboard talks to the launcher over Wi-Fi.

lines.text: The launcher talks to the rocket over a serial wire.
Inside the rocket, an ESP32 reads a motion sensor and moves four small canards.
lines.say: Inside the rocket, an E.S.P. thirty-two reads a motion sensor, and moves four small canards.

lines.text: Its one job would be to stop the roll.
No steering. No guidance. Just steady.
Normal procedures start without hardware.
The safest first experiment is reading the record.
Python 3.11 or newer. Run status. Run check.
lines.say: Python three eleven, or newer. Run status. Run check.

lines.text: Build the review, verify it, and open it in a browser.
Verification proves the packet is intact. Not that the rocket works.
Before power: ignition servo mechanically disconnected. No energetic material on the bench.
lines.say: Before power. Ignition servo, mechanically disconnected. No energetic material on the bench.

lines.text: Servos get their own supply, sized for stall current.
Wiring, verified. Firmware, built from a recorded commit.
Dashboard open, and labeled RAW SESSION, because it isn't evidence yet.
lines.say: Dashboard open, and labeled raw session, because it isn't evidence yet.

lines.text: Arm switch on: the launcher reaches READY.
lines.say: Arm switch on. The launcher reaches ready.

lines.text: Arm switch off: back to SAFE, and the abort is written down.
lines.say: Arm switch off. Back to safe, and the abort is written down.

lines.text: Ask the dashboard to launch…
It refuses.
Good.
Each canard has its own center angle in firmware, and a limit of twelve degrees either way.
Hold the rocket still and calibrate. The firmware won't confirm it; the dashboard only records that you asked.
lines.say: Hold the rocket still, and calibrate. The firmware won't confirm it. The dashboard only records that you asked.

lines.text: Then compare gains: one setting per session, the same fixture motion every time.
lines.say: Then compare gains. One setting per session, the same fixture motion every time.

lines.text: Close the dashboard cleanly. Declare what you did. Build a passport.
Then a named human decides whether it counts.
Software can organize evidence. It cannot accept it.
If rocket telemetry stops but the launcher keeps talking, open the status board and press DUMP LOG.
lines.say: If rocket telemetry stops, but the launcher keeps talking, open the status board, and press dump log.

lines.text: A reply clears the serial wire and the rocket, and points to the motion sensor.
Silence points to the wire or the rocket.
Every failure leaves a map.
Now the limits.
In its own model, the folding-fin linkage, as specified, doesn't close.
The spring margin is nineteen percent, against a twenty-percent requirement.
Two stability models disagree.
No physical measurement has been accepted. Not one.
The record keeps all of it. The contradiction is part of the result.
No claim has gone past the synthetic test. From here on, every gate needs a person.
Build a model. Make a prediction. Measure the difference. Keep the record honest.
Run the review.
